paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's house runs on God's terms, and He takes it seriously. The east gate stays shut because, as the LORD says, "the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it" (Ezekiel 44:2). Nobody gets to treat that place like a regular building, and Israel had done exactly that, so He says, "I have had enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel" (Ezekiel 44:6).

But look at what God does with the ones who wandered. The Levites who followed idols bear the consequences, and I think that stings, yet He still gives them work, saying, "I will appoint them to keep charge of all the work for the temple" (Ezekiel 44:14). Then the priests descended from Zadok, who kept charge of the sanctuary while Israel went astray, get to draw near to Him (Ezekiel 44:15). So faithfulness gets noticed, friend, and a messed-up past doesn't cancel a seat at the work.

And here's the part that got me: God tells the priests, "I am their inheritance" (Ezekiel 44:28), so no land, just HIM. Then He says to give the priest your first batch of dough "so that a blessing may rest upon your homes" (Ezekiel 44:30). So give God your first and your best, baker, and treasure Him over everything else. And the vision isn't over yet!
